title: Move to the bathroom
description: Navigate urgency, privacy, and safe movement in a narrow space.
learningObjective: Understand how urgency, visibility, support, and privacy affect bathroom safety.
context: Mr. Lim needs to move to the bathroom, a private activity where he may still want to manage independently.
challenges: Bathroom movement can involve urgency, narrow spaces, poor visibility, and embarrassment about needing help. These factors can increase pressure and make safe movement harder.
taskDescription: I need the bathroom, and I can feel myself wanting to hurry. Rushing is exactly when I'm most likely to lose my footing in a space this narrow. I want to get there safely, on my own if I can.

tasks.label: Switch on light
tasks.correctReason: Switching on the light first improves my visibility before I move through a narrow space.
tasks.warning: Lighting is the first safety issue. Moving in dim light makes it harder for me to judge distance and obstacles.

tasks.label: Hold grab rail
tasks.correctReason: Holding support improves my balance while I manage the urgency and my limited mobility.
tasks.warning: The grab rail helps, but poor lighting still increases the chance I misjudge the narrow space.

tasks.label: Enter bathroom
tasks.correctReason: Entering the bathroom is safer now because I already have visibility and physical support in place.
tasks.warning: I rushed toward the bathroom before improving visibility or holding support. The urgency increased my fall risk.

warnings.stool: Lighting is the first safety issue. Moving in dim light makes it harder for me to judge distance and obstacles.
warnings.walker: The grab rail helps, but poor lighting still increases the chance I misjudge the narrow space.
warnings.kettle: I rushed toward the bathroom before improving visibility or holding support. The urgency increased my fall risk.

completion: Safe sequence completed: the light is on, I have support, and I can enter the bathroom more safely.
feedbackTitle: You completed the bathroom navigation scenario.
feedback: Bathroom movement can be emotionally sensitive because it combines urgency, privacy, and physical risk. Rushing can make a familiar space dangerous. How a caregiver responds here says as much about respect as it does about safety — support that's available but not intrusive helps Mr Lim keep his dignity intact.
summary: Safe bathroom support balances visibility, physical stability, urgency, privacy, and dignity.
insight: A caregiver can improve lighting, install or encourage use of grab rails, and offer help in a way that protects privacy and dignity.
impacts: Advantage: better lighting reduces uncertainty and trip risk
Advantage: grab rails support balance in narrow areas
Disadvantage: taking time may feel stressful during urgency
Disadvantage: accepting help with bathroom routines can feel embarrassing
